questions.q: Order: salutation, subject, receiver's address, sender's address, date.
questions.a: sender's → date → receiver's → subject → salutation. A wrong answer putting subject first shows the student knows pieces, not positions — format marks are positional.

questions.q: A letter opens 'Dear Madam' and closes 'Yours sincerely' — what's wrong?
questions.a: The pairing — 'Dear Madam' (name unknown) locks to 'Yours faithfully'. A wrong answer 'nothing' shows the pairing contract isn't learned.

questions.q: Write the subject line for: inquiry about computer courses at an institute.
questions.a: Something like 'Inquiry regarding computer courses offered' — noun-phrase, one line. A wrong answer writing a full sentence ('I want to know about…') makes the subject a sentence, not a headline.

questions.q: The formal letter skeleton carries dedicated format marks: sender's address → date → receiver's address → subject → salutation → ______ body (purpose → details → request) → subscription → name.

Fill in the blank: The formal letter skeleton carries dedicated format marks: sender's address → date → receiver's address → subject → salutation → three-paragraph body (purpose → details → request) → ______ → name. 'Dear Sir/Madam' pairs with 'Yours faithfully'; named recipients pair with 'Yours sincerely'.

Fill in the blank: Think like the receiver: who is ______ (sender) → when (date) → who am I (receiver) → what about (subject, one line, noun-phrase) → greeting → body → sign-off matching the greeting.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student produces the 8-element skeleton in legal order for complaints/inquiries/letters-to-editor, pairs salutation↔subscription correctly, and audits defective letters for missing blocks.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Think like the receiver: who is writing (sender) → when (date) → who am I (receiver) → what about (subject, one line, noun-phrase) → greeting → body → sign-off ______ the greeting.
